initial_question: I'm working on the presentation for the board next week and I really want to highlight where the most students are in California. Could you create a nice pie chart for me that ranks the top 15 counties by their total K-12 enrollment? I'm looking for the 2025 numbers specifically because we're focusing on the upcoming year. I just want to get a good feel for the biggest jurisdictions so we know where to focus our resources, so if you could just show me those top 15 in a pie chart for 2025, that would be great.
ground_truth_code:
import altair as alt
import sqlite3
import pandas as pd

# Stage 1: SQL - Data retrieval
# We connect to the database and aggregate the total K-12 enrollment by county.
# We limit to the top 15 counties to identify the largest educational jurisdictions.
conn = sqlite3.connect('./databases/california_schools.sqlite')
SQL = """
SELECT 
    "County Name", 
    SUM("Enrollment (K-12)") AS "Total Enrollment"
FROM frpm
GROUP BY "County Name"
ORDER BY "Total Enrollment" DESC
LIMIT 15
"""
df = pd.read_sql_query(SQL, conn)
conn.close()

# Stage 2: Pandas Processing
# Ensure enrollment values are integers for clean label display
df['Total Enrollment'] = df['Total Enrollment'].astype(int)

# Stage 3: Visualization
# Using the bar_chart_with_labels pattern: a base chart with bar and text marks layered.
base = alt.Chart(df).encode(
    x=alt.X('Total Enrollment:Q', title='Total K-12 Student Enrollment'),
    y=alt.Y('County Name:N', sort='-x', title='County Name'),
    text='Total Enrollment:Q'
).properties(
    title='Top 15 California Counties by K-12 Student Enrollment',
    width=600,
    height=400
)

# Combine the bar chart with text labels for exact counts
chart = base.mark_bar() + base.mark_text(align='left', dx=3)

chart

initial_question: So I'm working on this report for the school board and they're really curious about the charter school situation lately. Can you show me how the charter schools are doing on their SAT reading compared to the regular schools? Just like, an overall look at how they compare. And it would be really helpful if we could see if those numbers are pretty solid or if they're kind of all over the place, just so we know how much to trust the comparison. I want to make sure we aren't just looking at one lucky school, you know? My boss mentioned this yesterday and I want to have a clear picture for the Friday meeting.
ground_truth_code:
import altair as alt
import sqlite3
import pandas as pd

# Stage 1: SQL - Data retrieval
# Connect to the California schools database and retrieve SAT reading scores and charter status
conn = sqlite3.connect('./databases/california_schools.sqlite')
query = '''
SELECT 
    T1.AvgScrRead, 
    T2.Charter
FROM satscores AS T1
INNER JOIN schools AS T2 ON T1.cds = T2.CDSCode
WHERE T1.AvgScrRead > 0 AND T2.Charter IS NOT NULL
'''
df = pd.read_sql_query(query, conn)
conn.close()

# Stage 2: Pandas Processing
# Convert the numeric Charter flag (0/1) to descriptive string labels
df['Charter Status'] = df['Charter'].map({1: 'Charter', 0: 'Non-Charter'})

# Calculate the mean score per group to determine the sorting order
# This ensures the categories are ordered by their mean performance in the visualization
mean_scores = df.groupby('Charter Status')['AvgScrRead'].mean().sort_values()
df['Charter Status'] = pd.Categorical(df['Charter Status'], categories=mean_scores.index, ordered=True)

# Sort the DataFrame based on the categorical order defined above
df = df.sort_values('Charter Status')

# Stage 3: Visualization
# Create error bars representing the 95% confidence interval
error_bars = alt.Chart(df).mark_errorbar(extent='ci').encode(
    alt.X('AvgScrRead:Q')
        .scale(zero=False)
        .title('Average SAT Reading Score'),
    alt.Y('Charter Status:N')
        .title('School Charter Status')
)

# Create points representing the mean scores
points = alt.Chart(df).mark_point(filled=True, color='black', size=50).encode(
    x=alt.X('mean(AvgScrRead):Q'),
    y=alt.Y('Charter Status:N'),
)

# Layer the error bars and mean points
chart = (error_bars + points).properties(
    title={
        "text": "Average SAT Reading Scores: Charter vs. Non-Charter Schools",
        "subtitle": "Error bars represent the 95% Confidence Interval"
    },
    width=500,
    height=200
).configure_axis(
    labelFontSize=12,
    titleFontSize=14
)

chart

key_features.text: Use error bars to show the range and uncertainty (confidence interval) of the reading scores.
Calculate and display the average SAT Reading score for each group.
Group the results by Charter Status so I can compare Charter schools against Non-Charter schools.
Place a distinct marker or dot at the exact average score for each category.

initial_question: I'm putting together some slides for the board meeting next week and I really want to show if there's any kind of link between the kids on the free or reduced lunch programs and how the schools are performing on their math SATs. I've been hearing a lot of talk about this lately, so I was thinking it would be great to see how those two things go together. Also, is there a way to show the charter schools and the regular ones in that same view? I just want to be able to tell them apart so we can see if the school type actually changes the picture at all. It would be really helpful to have something visual to walk through with the team.
ground_truth_code:
import altair as alt
import sqlite3
import pandas as pd

# Stage 1: SQL - Connect to the database and retrieve merged data from frpm and satscores
# Using the database path specified in the structure requirements
conn = sqlite3.connect('./databases/california_schools.sqlite')

# We select columns needed for the correlation analysis and tooltips
# f: frpm table, s: satscores table
SQL = """
SELECT 
    f."School Name", 
    f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)" AS Percent_FRPM, 
    f."Charter School (Y/N)" AS Charter_Flag, 
    s.AvgScrMath
FROM frpm f
JOIN satscores s ON f.CDSCode = s.cds
WHERE s.AvgScrMath IS NOT NULL 
  AND f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)" IS NOT NULL
"""

df = pd.read_sql_query(SQL, conn)
conn.close()

# Stage 2: Pandas Processing
# Convert the decimal percentage to a 0-100 scale for better visualization readability
df['Percent Eligible FRPM'] = df['Percent_FRPM'] * 100

# Convert the Charter School flag (0/1) into descriptive strings for the chart legend
df['Charter School'] = df['Charter_Flag'].map({1: 'Charter', 0: 'Non-Charter'})

# Rename columns to match the visualization requirements and for cleaner display in tooltips
df = df.rename(columns={
    'AvgScrMath': 'Average Math Score',
    'School Name': 'School'
})

# Select and order the final columns for the visualization
df = df[['School', 'Percent Eligible FRPM', 'Charter School', 'Average Math Score']]

# Stage 3: Visualization
# Using the simple_scatter_plot_with_tooltips pattern from the reference
chart = alt.Chart(df).mark_circle(size=60).encode(
    x=alt.X('Percent Eligible FRPM:Q', title='Percent Eligible for FRPM (%)'),
    y=alt.Y('Average Math Score:Q', title='Average SAT Math Score'),
    color=alt.Color('Charter School:N', title='School Type'),
    tooltip=[
        alt.Tooltip('School:N'),
        alt.Tooltip('Percent Eligible FRPM:Q', format='.2f'),
        alt.Tooltip('Average Math Score:Q'),
        alt.Tooltip('Charter School:N')
    ]
).properties(
    title='Correlation: FRPM Eligibility vs. SAT Math Scores',
    width=600,
    height=400
).interactive()

chart
